text:
Nina: dropping a new compact timeline mock for deployment history — goal: single-line entries, quick diff peek, and obvious canary/A-B signals. figma: https://figma.redwood/compact-rollout
Leo: looks promising. question: how will users start a revert? inline button or open detail flyout?
Nina: inline primary action opens a confirm flyout. want to keep the line uncluttered with only 1-2 controls: 'Details' chevron and an overflow menu for actions.
Priya: UX nit: overflow menu must be reachable by keyboard and show full action labels, not icons only. e.g., 'Restore this deployment' vs just 'Restore'.
Sam: product note: PMs prefer the term "Restore" because it's softer. ops docs and audit events currently use `rollback`. we should avoid confusing people.
Jamie: engineer here — we can map friendly labels to raw verbs. show friendly terms in UI, and include the raw verb under "Technical details" in the flyout.
Priya: accessibility: ensure the action button has aria-haspopup and an accessible name. Also add aria-live for success/failure messages after a restore.
Leo: for canaries, proposed visual: tiny pill with percent (e.g., "10%"), a small label 'canary' hidden visually but available to screen readers. That keeps lines compact.
Nina: yes — pill is tappable to expand allocation controls. inside the panel have both the slider and number input. keep a big helpful label: "Canary allocation".
Sam: implementation detail: slider needs to sync with number input and persist only when 'Save' clicked. watch for race conditions when autoscaling changes traffic mid-edit.
Jamie: confirmation flow idea: show a 20s countdown with 'Cancel' and 'Force now' options. countdown displays progress bar and remains keyboard-accessible. if user hits 'Force now' we call the `rollback` API with force=true.
Priya: keyboard focus rules: trap focus in the modal, return focus to the deployment row after completion, and announce status: "Restore complete: version 42 is now live." via aria-live.
Leo: microcopy suggestion for the modal header: "Restore deployment". body: "This will switch traffic and config to version 42. In-flight requests may be affected. This does not delete versions." primary: "Restore now" secondary: "Cancel".
Nina: alternate copy: "Switch to version 42" — shorter for mobile. which do we prefer?
Sam: ops prefers "Switch" in quick-flows. UX prefers "Restore" for clarity. maybe use "Switch" on compact controls and "Restore" in the modal.
Jamie: note for audit logs: always include the raw action name and parameters: `action: rollback`, `force: true` so support teams can trace it.
Priya: A/B tests: show variant chips 'A' and 'B' plus a tiny metric badge (e.g., latency: 120ms). chips need aria-describedby linking to the metric explanation.
Leo: diff preview: inline 1-line human-readable summary like "env: LOG_LEVEL changed: INFO -> DEBUG, max_workers: 8 -> 12". expand for full JSON in a monospace panel.
Nina: animation: subtle pulse on the row while countdown active; for users who set prefers-reduced-motion, show a static border instead. Put motion toggle in profile prefs.
Jamie: design accessibility checklist: contrast >= 4.5:1 for text, focus ring visible at 3px min, tooltips must be reachable by keyboard and dismiss on Escape.
Priya: also ensure color isn't the only indicator for status; add icons and text labels.
Sam: can we add an undo window after a restore (e.g., 5 minutes)? backend needs to support quick re-promote. If yes, show an inline snackbar with "Undo" button.
Jamie: backend can support a short automatic rollback window if enabled. we'll need to surface whether an environment has 'quick-undo' enabled.
Nina: action items: Leo to tighten chip spacing and iconography, Priya to draft aria labels and live-region text, Jamie to confirm API params and undo window feasibility, Sam to write final modal copy variants. I'll update figma and loop back.
ci-bot: CI: rollout-compact-ui branch build passed — 9 changed files (design tokens update).
Nina: thanks team — will bring these to design review on Thursday. :sparkles:
